page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-32 is a compute-skewed virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by Intel Xeon processors operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). The processor subsystem features a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction sets including AVX-512 Foundation and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized arithmetic. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB, establishing a lean 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation. The instance does not feature local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results characterize the instance by mid-tier multi-threaded throughput contrasted with modest single-core execution speed. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput registers in the lower quartile, mirrored by a Geekbench single-core score of 1150.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 23.79 GB/sec. When parallelized across all 32 vCPUs, execution scales to average industry tiers, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 29778.72, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9659.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 28275.53. Memory throughput remains steady under load, recording 177.33 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 91.03 GB/sec in write operations. In operational workloads, the instance processes 26.92 million Redis SET operations per second and handles lightweight 135M-parameter language model text generation at a strong rate of 284.06 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is focused on compute density rather than memory-heavy or local storage footprint. Because local disk storage is not bundled, operational costs depend on external persistent disks or network block storage. The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio limits utility for datasets requiring substantial memory capacity, but reduces overhead expenses associated with idle RAM. The instance fits high-concurrency, CPU-bound tasks such as parallel compilation via Clang, distributed CI/CD builds, batch transcoding, web proxying, and multi-threaded data transformation.

The architecture integrates AVX-512 vector instructions alongside 32.0 GB of memory, resulting in a dense 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled, requiring external network block storage for persistent data. Performance benchmarks reveal modest single-core speeds balanced by consistent average multi-core throughput, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 28275.53 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 70.83 GB/sec.
